name: Disaggregated LLM Serving (Prefill vs. Decode Pools)
tagline: Isolate compute-bound prompt prefill from HBM-bandwidth-bound token decode across dedicated GPU pools connected via RDMA/NVLink KV transfer.
purpose: Eliminate prefill-decode interference so long RAG prompts do not spike inter-token latency (ITL) for active streaming users.

spark.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving separates prompt prefill (compute-bound TTFT) and autoregressive token decode (HBM-bandwidth-bound ITL) onto independent GPU pools, transferring computed KV-cache blocks over RDMA or NVLink without stalling in-flight decode batches.
spark.keyTakeaway: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, prefill and decode sit on opposite sides of the GPU Roofline model; colocating them forces long prompts to stall every streaming decode user, whereas disaggregating lets each pool scale and parallelize independently.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** LLM inference splits into two physics-opposite phases: **Prefill** (compute-bound GEMMs over all prompt tokens, governing Time-to-First-Token `TTFT`) and **Decode** (HBM-bandwidth-bound single-token generation, governing Inter-Token Latency `ITL`). Colocating both on one GPU causes 16K-token prefills to freeze active decode streams.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts `Prompt Queue` -> `Prefill Pool (Compute-Bound GPUs)` -> `RDMA / NVLink KV Transfer` (`KV Blocks` transferred without stalling decode) -> `Decode Pool (HBM-Bandwidth-Bound GPUs)` running `Continuous Batching (ITL < 25ms)` -> `SSE Client`, achieving `Zero Prefill-Decode Interference`.

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Disaggregation requires high-bandwidth interconnects (`InfiniBand RDMA` or `NVLink`) so KV transfer time stays below `TTFT` budgets, and allows asymmetric tensor/pipeline parallelism (e.g., high TP on Prefill, high DP/batching on Decode).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Bound KV-transfer queues with admission backpressure and fall back to local chunked prefill if RDMA links degrade.

learningJourney.title: Prefill vs. Decode Physics & Disaggregated Pools
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand why separating compute-bound prefill and bandwidth-bound decode unlocks strict TTFT and ITL SLOs.

explanation.foundation: In a standard colocated vLLM/TensorRT-LLM replica, a single scheduler interleaves prompt prefill and autoregressive decode on the same GPUs. **Prefill** processes `N` prompt tokens in parallel (`O(N)` matrix-matrix multiplications), saturating Tensor Core FLOPs. **Decode** generates 1 token per sequence per step, streaming model weights and KV-cache from HBM (`HBM-bandwidth-bound`).
explanation.core: **Disaggregated serving** (used in DistServe, Splitwise, and Mooncake) assigns dedicated **Prefill GPUs** to compute the initial KV-cache and first token, streams the KV-cache blocks asynchronously over **RDMA / NVLink** (`mooncake` / `NIXL`), and hands the sequence to **Decode GPUs** optimized for large continuous batches.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Disaggregated LLM Serving (Prefill vs. Decode Pools), watch how prefill vs. decode physics & disaggregated pools interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Disaggregated LLM serving separates prompt prefill (compute-bound TTFT) and autoregressive token decode (HBM-bandwidth-bound ITL) onto independent GPU pools, transferring computed KV-cache blocks over RDMA or NVLink without stalling in-flight decode batches.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Disaggregated LLM Serving (Prefill vs. Decode Pools) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, prefill and decode sit on opposite sides of the GPU Roofline model; colocating them forces long prompts to stall every streaming decode user, whereas disaggregating lets each pool scale and parallelize independently.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: KV-Cache Transfer Budgeting, Layer-Wise Pipelining & Fallback
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: overlap KV-block transfers with layer computation and bound transfer queues.

explanation.foundation: Think of **KV-Cache Transfer Budgeting, Layer-Wise Pipelining & Fallback** as the intuition layer for Disaggregated LLM Serving (Prefill vs. Decode Pools): Operational control: overlap KV-block transfers with layer computation and bound transfer queues.
explanation.core: Overlap **layer-wise KV transfer** (`NIXL` / `GPUDirect RDMA`) so Layer `i`'s KV blocks begin transferring while Prefill computes Layer `i+1`. Pair with **prefix caching** on the Prefill pool so shared system prompts are neither recomputed nor re-transferred when the Decode pool already holds those KV block hashes.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, kv-cache transfer budgeting, layer-wise pipelining & fallback becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Disaggregated LLM serving separates prompt prefill (compute-bound TTFT) and autoregressive token decode (HBM-bandwidth-bound ITL) onto independent GPU pools, transferring computed KV-cache blocks over RDMA or NVLink without stalling in-flight decode batches.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
def estimate_kv_transfer_ms(layers: int, kv_heads: int, head_dim: int, seq_len: int, bytes_per_elem: int, link_gbps: float) -> float:
    """Compute theoretical KV-cache transfer time between Prefill and Decode pools."""
    if link_gbps <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Interconnect bandwidth must be positive")
    total_bytes = 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * seq_len * bytes_per_elem
    bytes_per_sec = (link_gbps * 1e9) / 8.0
    return (total_bytes / bytes_per_sec) * 1000.0
```

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does colocating a 32K-token RAG prompt prefill with active chat decode streams spike Inter-Token Latency (ITL)?

options.text: The 32K prompt prefill saturates Tensor Core compute for hundreds of milliseconds, delaying the next decode step for all active streams
options.feedback: Correct: colocated scheduling stalls decode iterations whenever a large unchunked prefill runs.

options.text: Decode requires more FP32 FLOPs than prefill
options.feedback: Incorrect: decode is HBM-bandwidth-bound, whereas prefill is compute-bound.

options.text: SSE connections drop whenever KV-cache exceeds 1 GB
options.feedback: Incorrect: SSE stays open; the latency spike comes from GPU compute preemption.

knowledgeChecks.question: What hardware capability is critical for disaggregated LLM serving at long context lengths (16K–64K)?

options.text: High-bandwidth RDMA / NVLink interconnect so KV-cache block transfer completes within a few milliseconds
options.feedback: Correct: transferring hundreds of MB of KV-cache per request over slow 10 Gbps Ethernet would blow the TTFT budget.

options.text: NVMe swap space replacing GPU HBM during decode
options.feedback: Incorrect: NVMe is orders of magnitude slower than HBM and would ruin ITL.

options.text: Disabling continuous batching on the Decode pool
options.feedback: Incorrect: the Decode pool relies on continuous batching to maximize HBM arithmetic intensity.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does prefix caching reduce cross-pool network traffic in a disaggregated cluster?

options.text: If the Decode worker already caches the shared system-prompt KV blocks by hash, Prefill only transfers the newly computed user-suffix blocks
options.feedback: Correct: skipping transfer of already-cached prefix blocks cuts RDMA traffic proportionally.

options.text: It converts FP8 weights to FP32
It removes the attention mechanism from layers 1–16
options.feedback: Incorrect: prefix caching reuses exact KV tensors without dropping layers.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: choose disaggregation for high-QPS long-context clusters with RDMA, not single-node deployments.
learningJourney.explanation: Adopt disaggregated serving when serving **long-context RAG, coding assistants, or agentic workloads** across multi-node InfiniBand/RoCEv2 clusters with strict `TTFT` + `ITL` SLAs. For small single-node 8B deployments or <1K-token prompts, colocated **chunked prefill** avoids network KV-transfer complexity.

learningJourney.title: KV-Cache Transfer Budgeting, Layer-Wise Pipelining & Fallback
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: overlap KV-block transfers with layer computation and bound transfer queues.
learningJourney.explanation: Overlap **layer-wise KV transfer** (`NIXL` / `GPUDirect RDMA`) so Layer `i`'s KV blocks begin transferring while Prefill computes Layer `i+1`. Pair with **prefix caching** on the Prefill pool so shared system prompts are neither recomputed nor re-transferred when the Decode pool already holds those KV block hashes.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
def estimate_kv_transfer_ms(layers: int, kv_heads: int, head_dim: int, seq_len: int, bytes_per_elem: int, link_gbps: float) -> float:
    """Compute theoretical KV-cache transfer time between Prefill and Decode pools."""
    if link_gbps <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Interconnect bandwidth must be positive")
    total_bytes = 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * seq_len * bytes_per_elem
    bytes_per_sec = (link_gbps * 1e9) / 8.0
    return (total_bytes / bytes_per_sec) * 1000.0
```

learningJourney.title: Colocated Chunked Prefill vs. Disaggregated Serving
learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: balance interconnect cost against independent prefill/decode autoscaling.
learningJourney.explanation: Colocated chunked prefill minimizes hardware fragmentation on small clusters, whereas disaggregation maximizes SLA goodput and lets you autoscale Prefill GPUs separately from Decode GPUs.

benefits: Zero network KV-transfer overhead; works over standard Ethernet.
costs: Prefill and decode compete for HBM bandwidth and SM compute; mixed workloads degrade goodput.

benefits: Zero prefill-decode interference; independent TP/batching and autoscaling per phase.
costs: Requires high-speed RDMA/NVLink and distributed KV-block registry coordination.

learningJourney.title: KV-Aware Router + Mooncake/NIXL Disaggregated Pool
learningJourney.purpose: Production architecture: route prompts by prefix-cache affinity and stream KV blocks over RDMA.
learningJourney.explanation: A **KV-aware gateway router** hashes the prompt prefix to pick a Prefill worker with warm prefix blocks, streams newly computed KV blocks via GPUDirect RDMA to an available Decode worker with free PagedAttention slots, and fails over to local chunked prefill if RDMA congestion exceeds threshold.

advanced.finalSummary: Prefill and decode sit on opposite sides of the GPU Roofline model; colocating them forces long prompts to stall every streaming decode user, whereas disaggregating lets each pool scale and parallelize independently.
advanced.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving separates prompt prefill (compute-bound TTFT) and autoregressive token decode (HBM-bandwidth-bound ITL) onto independent GPU pools, transferring computed KV-cache blocks over RDMA or NVLink without stalling in-flight decode batches.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, prefill and decode sit on opposite sides of the GPU Roofline model; colocating them forces long prompts to stall every streaming decode user, whereas disaggregating lets each pool scale and parallelize independently.
